# gddlm: Robust double linear models using gamma divergence

<!-- badges: start -->

[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://www.tidyverse.org/lifecycle/#experimental)

<!-- badges: end -->

`gddlm` is an `R` package associated with the manuscript "Robust double linear models using gamma divergence" by [Hui](https://francishui.netlify.app/), and [Sugusawa](https://sites.google.com/view/ssugasawa/), which is currently in preparation.

# Installation

Currently, `gddlm` is available and can be installed from Github with the help of `pak` package using:

```         
pak::pkg_install("fhui28/gddlm")
```

<!-- Alternatively, or if the above does not work, you may download a (hopefully!) stable release of `COQUE` by choosing the latest release on the right hand side of this Github webpage. -->

# Getting started and example usage

Please check the help files for the main `gddlm` and `gddlm_lsa` functions after installation. Alternatively, you can follow the basic example below.

```{r message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(mgcv)
library(mvtnorm)
library(gratia)
library(gddlm)
```

Simulate data from a double linear model with (average 5%) outliers in the response variable

```{r}
set.seed(112026)
n <- 500
p <- 10
H <- abs(outer(1:p, 1:p, "-"))
H <- 0.75^H
X <- cbind(1, rmvnorm(n, sigma = H))
Beta_true <- c(-1, -1, 1, -0.5, 0.5, 0.2, -0.2, rep(0, p - 6))
Delta_true <- c(0.5, 0.5, 0, 0, -0.5, 0, 0, 0.25, -0.25, rep(0, p - 8))

## Generate responses
mu_true <- as.vector(X %*% Beta_true)
sig_true <- exp(as.vector(X %*% Delta_true))
Y <- rnorm(n, mean = mu_true, sd = sig_true)

## Create outliers
om <- 0.05
out <- rbinom(n, 1, om)
Y[out==1] <- Y[out==1] + 50

hist(Y, breaks = 20)
```


Fit gamma divergence double linear models, select the gamma tuning parameter via cross-validation

```{r}
make_mu_formula <- paste0("response ~" , paste0("X", 1:p, collapse = " + ")) %>%
    formula
make_sigma_formula <- paste0("~" , paste0("X", 1:p, collapse = " + ")) %>%
    formula

runcv <- cv_gddlm(mu_formula = make_mu_formula,
                  sigma_formula = make_sigma_formula,
                  data = data.frame(response = Y, X[,-1]))

fit_gddglm_choosegamma <- gddlm(mu_formula = make_mu_formula,
                                sigma_formula = make_sigma_formula,
                                data = data.frame(response = Y, X[,-1]),
                                gamma_tuning = runcv$gamma_optimal_mean)
```


Demonstration of some of the functions available in the package

```{r}
fit_gddglm_choosegamma %>% 
    str

summary(fit_gddglm_choosegamma)

appraise(fit_gddglm_choosegamma)

coef(fit_gddglm_choosegamma)
coef(fit_gddglm_choosegamma, type = "sigma")

simulate(fit_gddglm_choosegamma, nsim = 10) %>% 
    str

predict(fit_gddglm_choosegamma, predictor = "mu", se.fit = TRUE) %>% 
    head
predict(fit_gddglm_choosegamma, predictor = "sigma", se.fit = TRUE) %>% 
    head
```



# If you find any bugs and issues...

If you find something that looks like a bug/issue, please use Github issues and post it up there. As much as possible, please include in the issue:

1.  A description of the bug/issue;
2.  Paste-able code along with some comments that reproduces the problem e.g., using the [reprex](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/reprex/index.html) package. If you also have an idea of how to fix the problem, then that is also much appreciated.
3.  Required data files etc...

Alternatively, please contact the corresponding author at [francis.hui\@anu.edu.au](mailto:francis.hui@anu.edu.au)
